description: A polyphonic arpeggiator: the notes played into it go into one shared list, and every channel of the Clock input runs its own arpeggio over that list

params.text: Switches between playing the note list in the order the notes arrived and playing it in pitch order, shown on the display as Time or Pitch
Chooses what the CV1 output carries: I keeps the CV1 voltage sampled as the note was played, C passes the present voltage of the note's own input channel, and O samples it on the output clock
Chooses what the CV2 output carries: I keeps the CV2 voltage sampled as the note was played, C passes the present voltage of the note's own input channel, and O samples it on the output clock
Steps forward through the play modes Up, Down, UpDn1, DnUp1, UpDn2, DnUp2 and Rand, and round again
Steps back through the play modes Up, Down, UpDn1, DnUp1, UpDn2, DnUp2 and Rand, and round again
Steps the octave range of the arpeggio up by one, from 1 to 4 octaves and round again
Steps the octave range of the arpeggio down by one, from 4 to 1 octaves and round again
Latches hold, so notes stay in the list after their gates fall, and lights while hold is on

inputs.text: A gate rising on a channel puts that channel's pitch into the note list, and its falling takes the note out again unless hold is on
The pitches played into the note list, at a volt per octave, taken from the channel whose gate has risen
A voltage carried along with the note played on the same channel and passed on at the CV1 output, as the S&H switch for CV1 sets
A voltage carried along with the note played on the same channel and passed on at the CV2 output, as the S&H switch for CV2 sets
Each rising edge moves that channel's arpeggio on by one note, and the number of channels here sets how many arpeggios run and the polyphony of every output
Adds its rounded voltage per channel to the play mode set by the buttons, so one output channel can run a different mode
Adds its rounded voltage per channel to the octave range set by the buttons, so one output channel can cover a different range
Adds its voltage per channel to the note order set by the button, so one output channel can run in the other order
A rising edge on a channel restarts that channel's arpeggio at the start of the list
Above 0.5V the hold setting is reversed, so notes are held while the Hold button is unlit and released while it is lit

outputs.text: Passes the gates of the Clock input on each channel while there are notes in the list
The pitch of the note that channel's arpeggio is playing, at a volt per octave
The voltage stored or sampled for the note that channel is playing, as the CV1 switch sets
The voltage stored or sampled for the note that channel is playing, as the CV2 switch sets

notes: with a monophonic Gate and V/Oct pair and hold in use, incoming notes are spread across the channels in turn, which lets patterns be entered from a sequencer
nothing comes out until a gate at the Gate input puts a note into the list and a clock at the Clock input steps the arpeggio; with Clock unpatched the outputs stay where they are

inputs.10: high above 0.5V · stepped · one channel only
